metadata.note: Ports and settlements that anchor Arctic shipping and basing.

properties.name: Murmansk
properties.note: Russia’s only large ice-free Arctic port, western terminal of the Northern Sea Route and base of the nuclear icebreaker fleet.

properties.name: Sabetta
properties.note: Purpose-built LNG port on the Yamal Peninsula, the commercial reason the route exists.

properties.name: Dudinka
properties.note: River port serving Norilsk’s nickel and palladium output.

properties.name: Tiksi
properties.note: Lena delta port and a reactivated Russian military airfield.

properties.name: Pevek
properties.note: Eastern Russian Arctic port, powered by a floating nuclear plant.

properties.name: Longyearbyen
properties.note: Svalbard’s main settlement. The archipelago is Norwegian, but the 1920 treaty gives signatories — including Russia — equal commercial access.

properties.name: Kirkenes
properties.note: Norwegian port on the Russian border, once pitched as a European rail head for Arctic shipping.

properties.name: Nuuk
properties.note: Capital of Greenland, the pivot of renewed strategic interest in the North Atlantic.

properties.name: Utqiaġvik
properties.note: Northernmost settlement in the United States, near the Bering approach to the route.
